title: Private PAC sample complexity from VC and Littlestone dimensions
formal: Is there a universal polynomial p such that every nonempty finite Boolean concept class C on a finite nonempty domain X admits a realizable, possibly improper PAC learner using some number $m\le p(1+\mathrm{VC}(C),1+\log^*\mathrm{LD}(C))$ of independent labeled examples, with error at most \(1/10\) and confidence at least \(9/10\), while satisfying $(1,1/(100m^2))$-differential privacy? The learning guarantee must hold for every distribution on the domain and every target concept in C. Computation time is unrestricted. Take both dimensions to be at least one; constant classes can be handled separately.
why: The problem seeks a privacy analogue of a foundational characterization theorem in learning theory.

progress.text: The survey gives lower bound $\Omega(\mathrm{VC}+\log^*\mathrm{LD})$ and upper bound $\min\{O(\log|C|),\widetilde O(\mathrm{LD}^5)\}$. The $\mathrm{VC}=1$ case is nearly understood; the general gap remains.

review_note: Concrete specialization of the quantitative target following Open Question 1: accuracy, confidence, epsilon, delta, and the meaning of polynomial overhead are fixed explicitly. The survey itself suppresses these parameters. Importance is editorial; cited proofs have not been independently audited.

context_blocks.text: VC dimension characterizes nonprivate learning. Finite Littlestone dimension $\mathrm{LD}$ characterizes the existence of private learning but does not determine its optimal quantitative cost.

A sample-complexity characterization should tell us how many labelled examples are necessary from the structure of the hypothesis class, rather than from a particular learning algorithm. Two classes can have the same ordinary capacity measure while differing in how difficult it is to hide the influence of an individual training example.

The quantitative issue matters even after learnability is settled. Knowing that some finite sample size works does not distinguish a useful bound from an enormous one. The proposed relation asks whether the extra price of privacy can be controlled by ordinary statistical complexity together with a very slowly growing function of online-learning complexity.

definitions: A concept class is a finite set of functions from a domain X to \(\{0,1\}\). \(\operatorname{VC}(C)\) is the largest size of a subset of X on which all binary labelings occur. \(LD(C)\) is the greatest depth of a complete binary tree labeled by domain points such that every root-to-leaf edge-label sequence is realized by a concept. The function log-star counts base-two logarithms needed to reach at most one. A learner may output a hypothesis outside C. Privacy requires $\Pr[A(S)\in E]\le e\Pr[A(S\prime)\in E]+1/(100m^2)$ whenever the two m-record samples differ by replacement of one record. Here X is finite, distributions on X are arbitrary probability vectors, and a learner is a probability kernel from length-m labeled samples to the finite set \(\{0,1\}^{X}\) of hypotheses. The sample size m is a positive integer chosen for C before the target and distribution. For every target \(h\in C\) and distribution D on X, with probability at least \(9/10\) over m independent draws \(x_{i}\) from D and learner randomness, the returned hypothesis has D-probability of disagreement with h at most \(1/10\). Privacy holds for all labeled samples, including unrealizable ones, and all subsets E of the hypothesis set. The same kernel and m work for all D,h. This finite-domain convention retains the finite-class target: points in an arbitrary domain with the same label vector \((h(x))_{h\in C}\) can be identified, giving at most \(2^{|}C|\) cells and preserving both dimensions. A learner on those cells lifts to the original domain. No running-time or computable-representation requirement is imposed.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.

importance.reason: Seeks a quantitative sample-complexity characterization of private learnability in terms of two basic dimensions, with consequences across hypothesis classes.

sentences: A private PAC learner must infer a Boolean concept from examples while limiting what its output reveals about any one example.
The reviewed question asks whether sample complexity is polynomial in VC dimension and the iterated logarithm of Littlestone dimension.
VC dimension measures ordinary statistical capacity, whereas Littlestone dimension measures how many adaptive prediction challenges the class can support.
A positive answer would bound the additional sample cost of privacy by a remarkably slow-growing contribution from that online complexity.

The saved formulation fixes constant accuracy and confidence, permits improper hypotheses and unlimited computation, and specifies approximate privacy with an additive privacy parameter shrinking quadratically in sample size.
